results.summary_before: This design implements an adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire neuron in Verilog, where the firing threshold adapts based on recent spike activity so that sustained input produces progressively fewer spikes. It accepts an 8-bit input current on ui_in, exposes an 8-bit membrane state variable on uo_out, and emits a spike on uio[7]. Testing is done with the provided test.py by applying varying input currents and comparing observed outputs against expected values. No external hardware is required, and the documentation is limited to a brief description and test instructions.

results.summary_before: This is an eight-part audio-visual megademo that outputs VGA graphics through the TinyVGA PMOD and PWM audio on the bidirectional pins. It runs at 25.175 MHz and is used by connecting a VGA monitor and speakers or the TT Audio PMOD. Silicon test reports confirm both VGA and audio work on multiple boards, with testers reporting it also runs at 32 MHz and even 66 MHz though monitors may not sync that fast. The documentation is thin, describing the design only as a compressed VGA logo, so the internal demo structure is not documented.

results.summary_before: This block is titled 83rk: Tiny Tapeout and implements an SR flip-flop using inputs a and b and presenting AND, NAND and OR outputs along with divided clocks on outputs 3 and 4. The documented test is simply to set and reset the flip-flop while checking the output values, and no external hardware is required. It runs in Wokwi with a 10000 Hz clock and the design is a simple combinational and sequential logic demonstration rather than a complete application. The documentation is very brief but consistent with the pin names.
